highlights.title: Sign in to ChatGPT and Grok in the app
highlights.text: From Get started, approve a short code in your browser and you're signed in. No Terminal needed. No Node? kwant still installs Codex and the bots' browser.

highlights.title: Recipes you can cook from
highlights.text: A recipe in a reply shows as a card with its ingredients and steps. Change the servings and the amounts follow. Oven temperatures stay as written.

highlights.title: Set up a Linux server in one line
highlights.text: One command installs kwant on a Linux server. It checks the download, never uses sudo and ends with your sign-in link: curl -fsSL https://kwant.si/install.sh | sh

highlights.title: Get started in three steps
highlights.text: A new person's #general opens with one card: Choose your AI, Sign in, Pick a team. Choosing an AI installs it when it's missing.

fixes: Take over says when you're already controlling the browser in another window, instead of retrying.
Undo for a ready-made team names the exact archived chat it keeps.
A Jira ticket whose lead can't prepare a brief says why, and what to change.
Show it once explains a failed draft or an empty trial reply in plain words.
A GitLab address without .git now works, just as a GitHub one does.
After "folder in use", a ready-made team's button says Pick another folder instead of Try again.
Telegram no longer says your message wasn't run when a routine or a Jira task hit today's spending stop.
A Linux server reports its real version, not 0.1.0.
